name: Mop Fly
imitates: A generic worm, cranefly larva or caddis larva silhouette; a bulky, fast-sinking mop-chenille fly that works for trout, carp and panfish.

steps.text: Put the bead on the hook and lay down a thread base behind it; a heavy slotted bead gets the fly down quickly.
Decide the mop body length; here it extends about one hook length past the bend. Trim it shorter for small-mouthed fish.
Put cement or super glue on top of the shank so the mop cannot spin, then tie the mop down with tight wraps (compress it or strip a little to reach the core) and add a drop of glue.

Add a dubbing collar: spread a small pinch of aligned dubbing around the hook and secure it with two or three tight wraps, repeating for a fuller collar. Whip finish behind the bead. The finished fly.
